results.title: Troubleshoot OOM events | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) | Google Cloud Documentation
results.snippet: In a Kubernetes environment, the OOM Killer operates at two different scopes: the control group (cgroup), which affects one container; and the system, which affects the entire node. A container-level OOM kill occurs when a container attempts to exceed its predefined memory limit.

results.title: What Everyone Should Know About Kubernetes Memory Limits, OOMKilled Pods, and Pizza Parties — Robusta Blog
results.snippet: To paraphrase Tim Hockin, one of the Kubernetes maintainers at Google, the best practice for Kubernetes resource limits is to set memory limit=request, and never set CPU limits to avoid Kubernetes CPU throttling.

results.title: How to Fix OOMKilled Kubernetes Error (Exit Code 137)?
results.snippet: The memory limit is the ceiling of RAM usage that a container can reach before it is forcefully terminated, whereas the memory request is the baseline amount of memory that Kubernetes will guarantee for the container’s operation. When a container attempts to consume more memory than its set limit the Linux OOM Killer changes the container status to ‘OOMKilled’, which prompts Kubernetes to terminate it.
